name: Cisco YANG Suite
what_it_is: A GUI-based Django web application for exploring YANG data models and performing NETCONF, RESTCONF, and gNMI operations against Cisco network devices. It supports dynamic plugin discovery, telemetry subscription, and YANG model browsing/diff operations.
components: yangsuite — core Django application (uWSGI, served via unix socket)
nginx — reverse proxy; redirects port 80 to 8443, serves static files
backup — cron-based backup container (configurable interval, default every 30 min)
measurement: gRPC model-driven telemetry (MDT) subscriptions via ports 57344–57345
YANG model browsing and diff between model versions
configuration: setup.env file (env_file) passed to the yangsuite container at compose time
yangsuite.ini for PIP installs: data_path, port, allowed_hosts, secret_key, settings_module, eula_agreement, dna_advantage
Plugin management via Admin → Manage plugins page or by placing plugin wheels in docker/yangsuite/ and rebuilding
start_yang_suite.sh prompts for superuser credentials and SSL/TLS certificate generation
YS_BACKUP_CRON env var (default: */30 * * * *) and YS_MAX_BACKUP (default: 2) control backup behavior
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection capability documented; the tool is an operations/exploration GUI, not a chaos/fault platform
modes: Docker Compose (recommended) — HTTPS on port 8443, nginx on port 80
PIP/Python venv — HTTP only on port 8480, no exposed ports
One-container-alternative — single container with no interactive setup required
constraints: Requires approximately 3.5 GB of memory to load large Cisco native YANG models
Python 3.9+ required for PIP install; Python 3.10 recommended
Docker install uses HTTPS; PIP install uses HTTP only (no TLS)
Self-signed certificates generated by start_yang_suite.sh are for testing only; production requires a CA-signed certificate
docker_services: nginx (custom build from ./nginx/Dockerfile, reverse proxy + static files)
backup (custom build from ./backup/Dockerfile, cron-based data backup)
notable_absences: No device simulator or emulator included — requires a real or separately-provisioned Cisco device target
No built-in CI/CD or test-runner framework
No database service declared in docker-compose (uses Django's default SQLite or file-based storage under ys-data volume)
No multi-user RBAC beyond a single Django superuser created at setup time
